extracted.intended_audience: neuroscience researchers and fMRI investigators studying laughter, vocalization and emotional motor systems
extracted.subtask_short: fMRI study of laughter and speech
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, acquiring and analysing an fMRI experiment that provokes tickle-induced laughter and/or voluntary vocalization to identify neural correlates of the competition between involuntary and voluntary vocalization. Includes participant selection, stimulus/timing design, acquisition parameters, preprocessing and statistical analysis procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion/exclusion and motion-based exclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the total 38 participants who volunteered, 30 were included (24 females, 6 males; mean age = 23.0 years; range 20–30). Two excluded for technical constraints during image acquisition. Six participants were excluded because "the number of displacements exceeding 1 were higher than a limit of 60% relative to the participant that showed the highest number of displacements exceeding 1."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scan-to-scan frame-displacements evaluated by summing the six head-movement parameters provided by SPM re-alignment (G motion parameters). The validity of this motion-based selection approach was verified in an earlier investigation on laughter (cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, consent and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The informed consent of all participants was obtained, and the procedure was approved by the Ethical Committee of the University Hospital of Greifswald, Germany (BB063/10a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional ethical approval and documented informed consent for human-subject fMRI experiments involving tactile stimulation and provoked laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-related experimental design with anticipation and treatment phases
rubrics_metrics.description: An event-related paradigm including effects of anticipation (A) and stimulus application (treatment, T). At onset of anticipation participants were encouraged to either remain silent (S) or produce regular 'ha' vocalizations (V); anticipation (A) was followed by treatment (T) where participants received either tickling or monotonous touch of the right foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define four conditions per participant (ToS, ToV, TiS, TiV) with randomized application of the two sensory stimulations during treatment. Use visual cues (smiley face to signal anticipation onset; red bar to inform tickler to start treatment) and vary anticipatory duration (jitter) to minimize habituation and improve unpredictability (variable anticipatory duration up to 10.4 s; min 5.4 s). Report number of events per condition and account for technical variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of behavioural/manipulation controls to reduce motion artefacts (barbecue stick)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce movement artefacts during fMRI image acquisition, participants were instructed to hold a wooden barbecue stick between their teeth to prevent jaw opening when laughing and thus triggering head movement. A pilot study confirmed the barbecue stick does not interfere with or restrict ability to laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying overt vocalizations or laughter, include validated physical restraints or procedures (with pilot verification) that limit motion without impairing the behaviour of interest to reduce susceptibility and signal loss at air–tissue/bone interfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio recording and post-processing for vocal-response labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded full experimental procedure with an fMRI-adapted fibre optic microphone. For every subject obtained a single audio file (~30 ± 5 min). After the experiment, Audacity® software 2.3.3 was used to reduce background noise and to label experimental events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MR-compatible microphones, denoise audio post hoc, and label events to evaluate vocal responses; keep continuous recordings covering the whole scan run for later segmentation and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter scoring/classification metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter during tickling classified as: 'weak' = strong expiration without an audible vocalization; 'middle' = bursts of laughter with only one audible vocalization; 'strong' = bursts of laughter with two or more audible vocalizations. The score reflects frequency and intensity of audible laughter events. In TiV (tickle + voluntary vocalization) only strong outbursts of laughter could be clearly identified by this method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear, reproducible operational criteria for coding laughter intensity in audio, and note limitations when voluntary vocalizations overlap with spontaneous laughter (reporting constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameter reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional BOLD acquisition on a 3 T Scanner with 32-channel head coil using a T2*-weighted EPI multiband sequence (TR = 900 ms; TE = 40.6 ms; flip angle = 54°; voxel size = 2.2 × 2.2 × 2.2 mm; slice thickness = 2.2 mm; matrix 64 × 64; 64 axial slices; multiband factor = 6). Additional 198 phase-and-magnitude images (TR = 666 ms; TE1 = 4.92 ms; TE2 = 7.38 ms; flip angle = 60°; resolution = 2 × 2 × 2 mm). Structural T1 MPRAGE (TR = 1690 ms; TE = 2.52 ms; flip angle = 9°; voxel size ≈ 0.97 × 0.97 × 1 mm). Collected 1475 EPIs per subject (total acquisition time 1327 s), with exceptions when fewer volumes were available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully report scanner, coil, sequence type, all timing and spatial resolution parameters, multiband factor and number of volumes per run; include any deviations per subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwarping, realignment and motion-correction preprocessing pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Unwrapping of geometrically distorted EPIs performed using a VDM (voxel displacement map) field map image. Each scan realigned to the scan with half-maximal displacement (translation/rotation parameters with highest maximal deviation). EPIs co-registered with T1-weighted anatomical image. T1 segmented and normalized to MNI template. EPIs resliced at 2.2 × 2.2 × 2.2 mm and smoothed with a 6 × 6 × 6 mm Gaussian kernel (FWHM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply field-map unwarping, robust realignment referencing a representative scan, co-registration with structural, segmentation/normalization to standard template and smoothing (report kernel). These steps aim to increase signal-to-noise and correct for geometric distortion and motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level GLM specification and artifact adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement parameters estimated during re-alignment were introduced as regressors into the general linear model (GLM). fMRI data additionally adjusted for artefacts by reduced weighting of motion-contaminated volumes using the RobustWLS toolbox. Event-related analysis modelled anticipation (A) and treatment (T) with a reaction and neuronal conduction time of 400 ms included in the modelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include motion regressors, use robust weighting or artifact down-weighting methods (e.g., RobustWLS) to mitigate motion-contaminated volumes, and explicitly model expected neural conduction/reaction delays (here 400 ms). Clearly define contrasts for each condition at first-level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast definitions and merging logic for anticipatory conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast images calculated for the four treatment conditions (ToS, ToV, TiS, TiV) and for anticipation. Because participants did not know during the anticipatory period whether they would be stimulated by tickling or touch, the two silent anticipatory conditions (AS) were merged, as were the two vocalization anticipation conditions (AV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When anticipatory cues do not uniquely signal subsequent stimulus type, merge equivalent anticipatory conditions to increase power and reflect uncertainty in the anticipatory period; document merging logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level group analysis design and contrast logic (2×2 ANOVA and conjunctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Task-related changes during treatment conditions investigated at group level by introducing contrast images into a 2 × 2 ANOVA. Regions activated in both tickling conditions identified by conjunction analysis of TiS with TiV. Specific effects identified by conjunctions of TiS > ToS & TiS > ToV (tickle > touch/voluntary vocalization) and TiV > ToS & TiV > ToV (tickle+voluntary vocalization > touch+voluntary vocalization). Also used 1 × 4 ANOVA for anticipatory contrasts and conjunction analyses opposing AS and AV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design second-level factorial ANOVAs to separate main effects and interactions, and use conjunction analyses to isolate regions reliably activated across related contrasts. Explicitly state which conjunctions/contrasts test which hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding and whole-brain inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Performed whole-brain analyses and extracted Z-scores from voxels that survived a familywise error (FWE) correction threshold of p < 0.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate multiple-comparison correction (here FWE p<0.05) for whole-brain voxelwise inference and report surviving clusters, peak coordinates, Z/t-scores and cluster sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioural rating measures and correlational analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants rated tickling as 'pleasant' (mean 7.18 ± 1.9 of 10) and 'rather ticklish' (mean 5.35 ± 2.1 of 10). Ticklishness correlated with laughter score (Kendall's tau-b reported). Kendall's tau-b used to correlate laughter scores between conditions (e.g., r = 0.506, p < 0.001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect subjective ratings of stimuli and relate them to objective behavioural measures (laughter counts/intensity); use nonparametric correlation (Kendall's tau-b) when appropriate and report effect sizes and p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of neuroanatomical results with standard coordinates and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported activated anatomical brain regions with hemisphere, cluster size (voxels), MNI coordinates (peak) and Z-scores in tables (e.g., Table 1 & Table 2) and illustrated activation maps in figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present comprehensive result tables listing regions, laterality, cluster sizes, peak MNI coordinates and Z/t-scores, and accompany with brain figures thresholded at the stated corrected p-value for clarity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability, supplementary materials and code sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic supplementary material available online (Figshare). Data underlying the final statistics available at https://github.com/NitramNimod/When-laughter-arrests-speech-fMRI-based-evidence. Electronic supplementary material and associated data citations are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide open access to supplementary materials, processed data and analysis code/links to repositories to enable reproducibility of fMRI findings.
